posts.text: Our new engineering blog shares how we migrated the Claude Messages API from Python to Rust. We share how we used the existing Python service to verify the migration, with teams of agents tracking down and fixing differences between the two versions. https://x.com/AnthropicAI/status/2125627317263466739?a=cMWx_Moml5Tb3-Enk4A&s=20
A robot arm plays 62 moves of checkers, correcting for its own 7mm sag.
What are you exploring with Fable 5.2?
It’s been two weeks since we released Claude Fable 5.2. Here’s what people have been exploring with it: Where the letter A came from, one alphabet at a time.
A practical guide to shipping with Claude Code: how to hand off PR follow-up work to Claude Ship and stay in flow. https://claude.dev/blog/the-work-after-you-open-a-pr/

You can now install Claude artifacts as desktop apps on Mac and Windows. Ask Claude to build an artifact, click "Install as app", and open it like any other app. It can use your connectors and, if you allow it, send notifications or add a menu bar item.

You don't have to package or sign the app, or set up an API key. Building the app and any calls it makes to Claude count toward your usage limits. It's in beta on all plans in Claude Desktop (on Enterprise, an owner needs to switch it on first). https://claude.com/resources/articles/install-as-app

Today's launches build on recent updates that make MCP in Claude more token efficient, easier to authorize, and more interactive. Thanks to the community, Claude now has over 10,000 MCP connectors. Read more: https://claude.com/blog/skills-over-mcp-tasks-and-more

With Tasks (GA), servers can run long operations or full agent loops while Claude keeps working and picks up the result when it's ready. File Uploads is also rolling out soon. Claude will be able to send PDFs, spreadsheets, and images to a server without passing them through the context window.

MCP turns two! What started as a protocol for connecting AI apps to tools and data is evolving to standardize how agents communicate and orchestrate work. We’re bringing more of these agentic capabilities to Claude with Skills over MCP and Tasks.

Claude Managed Agents is our platform for developers to build agents that are intelligent and secure. @jess__yan, @_hi_mc, and @RLanceMartin tell the product iteration story of how we redesigned its architecture. Watch the full conversation: https://youtu.be/8Aoq6mJeAXI

We've redesigned the side panel in Claude Code on desktop. Files, Changes, Terminal and your other tools now open as tabs beside your session. You can still move a tab to see several at once, or pop it out into its own window. Rolling out on Mac. Windows and Linux coming soon!

There’s now one way to connect your tools to Claude, teach it a new skill, or do both. Connectors and skills come together as plugins. Live on Free, Pro, Max, and Ultra plans, with Team and Enterprise coming soon. Browse 10,000+ plugins: https://claude.ai/plugins

On Team and Enterprise, admins can turn it on for a whole repo, so it runs on your team's PRs with no /ship needed. Your approval policy lives in the repo like a smarter CODEOWNERS file. Read more: https://claude.com/resources/articles/introducing-claude-ship
Introducing Claude Ship (beta): Claude can review your pull requests, work on fixes, and approve the ones your team's policy allows. The goal is to help you ship code as fast as you can write it.

Try it on your next PR: update Claude Code and run /ship. It's rolling out in the CLI and desktop app now. Claude opens the PR, reviews your change, and works on feedback and failing checks. Your permissions and branch rules still decide what can merge.

Zero data retention with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards is now in public beta for eligible orgs on the Claude Platform. Encrypted copies of your Messages API traffic go to your own cloud storage. Automated checks look for misuse and flag serious risks for your team to review.

You can turn it on per workspace in the Claude Console. It covers every Messages API request in that workspace, on any model. Docs: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/enterprise-frontier-safeguards/overview
EFS is available on the Claude Platform, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, and Claude on Google Cloud. Support for EFS in Microsoft Foundry is coming soon.

Zero data retention (ZDR) with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) is now in public beta for eligible businesses. It looks for misuse across many requests while remaining compatible with ZDR. We developed it with over 100 customers. Read more: https://claude.com/resources/articles/zero-data-retention-with-enterprise-frontier-safeguards

You can now opt into more frequent builds of Claude Desktop on Windows and Mac. Switch to the Latest release channel in Settings > Desktop app. You'll get fixes and improvements faster, but these builds can be less reliable than Stable, which stays the default.

Check out Code Mode, a new, experimental way for Claude Code to work with tools. Claude writes scripts that chain your tools together in sophisticated ways, and it can answer you while long commands are still running. Opt in with CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1 http://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode

Platforms can offer Claude without building their own metering or invoicing. They decide who pays on each request and can understand usage by customer. Customers can draw down an existing Anthropic commitment or pay as they go, and see spend by platform.

Linked billing is live today in beta with Asana, ClickHouse, Factory, Gumloop, Harness, Higgsfield AI, Kilo Code, Linear, Major, Mintlify, Niteshift, Omni, OpenArt, Railway, Ramp, Runlayer, Tessera, Tines and Warp. To add support or learn more: https://claude.com/blog/linked-billing-on-claude-platform

Linked billing is now in beta on the Claude Platform. Now users of tools like Factory, Linear, and Ramp can pay for Claude API usage through their Claude Platform organization, without sharing an API key.

Claude writes better code when it can verify its work. Checks that used to be expensive, like tests, benchmarks, and end-to-end runs, are now cheap. Here’s how the Claude Code team thinks about verification: https://claude.dev/blog/how-the-claude-code-team-thinks-about-verification/

Working in a terminal? The Xcode plugin is now in the official Claude Code plugin marketplace. Claude can use it to build, run, and test your app, render SwiftUI previews, and search developer docs. /plugin install xcode@claude-plugins-official

That $30 in sales from an hour of work is not profit. Food costs often take ~30% of revenue, labor another ~30%, then rent, utilities, equipment, marketing, insurance and taxes. Profit is the thin remainder after all of those. Economies of scale: bigger output lowers average cost per unit. Fixed costs (building, machines) get spread over more sales. Bulk buying cuts ingredient prices. McDonald’s makes each burger far cheaper than a small independent shop can.

The 796th MP Bn was a real US unit in Vienna that took part in the International Patrol. It is not the invented Allied Command “Militärpolizeilicher Dienst” or Austrian Wachbataillon Wien named in the Lachout text. Austria had no armed forces until 1955. The 1987 paper is a documented forgery.
